errors.text_span: The pie chart represents the distribution of 1.1K samples across nine capabilities, categorized into four groups.
errors.evidence: The chart is a two-level radial chart, not a standard pie chart. It shows three inner categories (Contradiction Resolution, Context Retrieving, Context Tracking) that group the nine outer capabilities, not four groups.

errors.text_span: including Context Tracking (dark blue), Recursive Reasoning (blue), Triggering (light blue), Dynamic Environment (navy blue), Memorization (blue-green), Dynamic Instruction (light teal), Context Retrieving (green), Multitasking (teal), and Privacy Protection (reddish-pink), and Contradiction Resolution (reddish-brown)
errors.evidence: This list incorrectly treats the three inner categories (Context Tracking, Context Retrieving, Contradiction Resolution) as if they are outer slices, on the same level as the other capabilities. This demonstrates a fundamental misunderstanding of the chart's structure.
The description omits two capabilities shown in the chart: "Prioritization" (value 100) and "Personalization" (value 100).

errors.text_span: The approximate proportions of the slices are: Context Tracking (14%), Recursive Reasoning (13%), Triggering (12%), Dynamic Environment (12%), Memorization (12%), Dynamic Instruction (12%), Context Retrieving (12%), Multitasking (19%), Privacy Protection (13%), and Contradiction Resolution (13%).
errors.evidence: This entire list of percentages is incorrect. It is based on a flawed understanding of the chart's structure and the values are numerically wrong. For example, Multitasking has a value of 160 out of a total of 981, which is approximately 16.3%, not 19%.
